title: channel_recent read endpoint + context (AdminRepo + explicit tenant filter, since/limit, live-only, oracle-safe)

story.as_a: coding agent starting or resuming work on a repo
story.i_want_to: read the recent, non-expired posts on my repo's channel, optionally only those since a timestamp
story.so_that: I can see what other sessions (on any machine) said or did without anyone hand-relaying it to me

rationale: This is the read half and the payload behind the SessionStart TEAM CHANNEL block. It must be strictly tenant+project scoped (AdminRepo + explicit tenant_id filter, the loopctl content pattern), cheap, return only live posts newest-first with a since delta, and never leak whether another tenant's project exists.

background.includes: Read scoping mirrors ProjectController agent-open, tenant-scoped reads; queried via AdminRepo + explicit tenant_id filter (NOT RLS Repo).

acceptance_criteria.description: GET /api/v1/channel/posts?project_id=&since=&limit= is RequireRole :agent, tenant-scoped from the key, and returns posts for that project_id. Ordering is CONDITIONAL on the delta mode (order_recent/2, lib/loopctl/coordination.ex:2286-2295): a NON-DELTA read (no since) orders inserted_at DESC, seq DESC; a DELTA read (since present AND no cursor) orders GREATEST(inserted_at, updated_at) DESC, seq DESC — the SAME expression the since filter uses (AC-39.3.3), because a keyed slot whose updated_at (not inserted_at) advanced past since MATCHES the filter yet, ordered by its stale inserted_at, would rank last among matched rows and be the FIRST row dropped by LIMIT — precisely the SessionStart working-state slot the bus exists to surface. (Epic 40 later added a keyset cursor OUTSIDE this story's parameter list, making three modes, not two: recent_page/3 NULLs since whenever a cursor is present — lib/loopctl/coordination.ex:1806 — so ?cursor=&since= is a HISTORY read and takes the non-delta inserted_at DESC, seq DESC clause; see AC-40.C2.4.) seq is the deterministic tie-breaker in both branches: a DB-side bigserial column (added by migration 20260718000000), mapped on the schema as field :seq, :integer, read_after_writes: true (lib/loopctl/coordination/channel_post.ex:198-201) — Ecto never generates it, it is read back from the sequence. Do NOT unify the two orderings: a re-touched slot is a DELTA concept, not a history concept (consistent with Epic 40 AC-40.C2.4). An OpenApiSpex operation/1 spec is declared (passes openapi_test.exs).
Only LIVE posts are returned: the query filters expires_at > now() defensively (independent of the sweep), so an expired-but-not-yet-swept post never appears.

since (ISO8601) filters to greatest(inserted_at, updated_at) > since (apply_since/2, lib/loopctl/coordination.ex:2223-2232) — with the caveat that the caller passes commit_lag_since(since) (coordination.ex:1813; helper :2239-2242), which subtracts @commit_lag_epsilon_seconds = 5 (:142), so the EFFECTIVE boundary is > since - 5s: a deliberate at-least-once overlap for commit lag (AC-40.C2.2), so a row touched within 5s BEFORE since is RE-RETURNED, not excluded, and the consumer dedups. limit defaults to 25 and is CLAMPED to a max of 100 (a larger value is clamped to 100, matching the read-bound convention — not a 400). MALFORMED since IS A NO-OP, NEVER AN ERROR: normalize_since/1 (coordination.ex:2207-2221) resolves an absent, malformed, or date-only (wrong-granularity) value to nil, which makes the filter a no-op so the caller gets the NEWEST PAGE under the non-delta ordering. Never a 500, never a 400, never a forced-empty list. An offset-less but otherwise valid ISO8601 instant (e.g. "2026-07-18T00:00:00") IS accepted and interpreted as UTC (parse_since/1, coordination.ex:2297+), because DateTime.from_iso8601/1 rejects it and silently disabling the delta would defeat the 'read only what's new' contract.

ORACLE-SAFE: a project_id belonging to another tenant, or a nonexistent project_id, returns 200 with an EMPTY list — UNIFORMLY, identical to an owned-but-empty project. It NEVER returns 404 and never a different status/body that would reveal whether the project exists in another tenant.

Each returned post includes id, agent_id, session_id, host, key, body, refs, inserted_at, updated_at — enough to render 'who / which machine / which session / when' and to self-dedupe by session_id. agent_id is the only server-stamped (authoritative) attribution; session_id/host are client-supplied and informational.
The response is a standard {data: [...], meta: {...}} envelope; meta carries the applied limit and returned count.
Query uses AdminRepo with an EXPLICIT tenant_id filter (never relies on RLS as the isolation mechanism), consistent with Knowledge/Projects reads.

acceptance_criteria_amendments.original_wording: GET /api/v1/channel/posts?project_id=&since=&limit= is RequireRole :agent, tenant-scoped from the key, and returns posts for that project_id ordered inserted_at DESC. An OpenApiSpex operation/1 spec is declared (passes openapi_test.exs).
acceptance_criteria_amendments.amended_wording: ... returns posts for that project_id with CONDITIONAL ordering: non-delta (no since, or a cursor present) orders inserted_at DESC, seq DESC; delta (since present AND no cursor) orders GREATEST(inserted_at, updated_at) DESC, seq DESC — the same expression the since filter uses.
acceptance_criteria_amendments.rationale: SPEC WAS WRONG, CODE IS RIGHT — no code change. The flat 'ordered inserted_at DESC' wording is correct only for the NON-DELTA branch. As shipped (order_recent/2, lib/loopctl/coordination.ex:2286-2295) the delta branch orders by GREATEST(inserted_at, updated_at) DESC, seq DESC, matching the AC-39.3.3 filter. Without that, a keyed working-state slot re-upserted after since matches the filter (its updated_at advanced) but ranks by its stale inserted_at — last among matched rows — and is the FIRST row LIMIT truncates, silently dropping the exact SessionStart slot the bus exists to surface. seq tie-breaks same-microsecond rows deterministically in both branches: a DB-side bigserial (migration 20260718000000) exposed on the schema as field :seq, :integer, read_after_writes: true (channel_post.ex:198-201, bigserial rationale comment :198-200). The delta rule is 'since present AND no cursor', not simply 'since present': Epic 40's keyset cursor (outside this story's parameter list) NULLs since when a cursor is supplied (recent_page/3, coordination.ex:1806), so ?cursor=&since= is a HISTORY read on the non-delta clause — three modes, not two. The two orderings are deliberately NOT unified: a re-touched slot is a delta concept, not a history-cursor concept — the same split Epic 40 already documents at us_40.c2.json AC-40.C2.4, kept consistent here.

acceptance_criteria_amendments.original_wording: since (ISO8601) filters to greatest(inserted_at, updated_at) > since; limit defaults to 25 and is CLAMPED to a max of 100 (a larger value is clamped to 100, matching the read-bound convention — not a 400).
acceptance_criteria_amendments.amended_wording: ... plus: a malformed, absent, or date-only since resolves to nil — a NO-OP filter that returns the newest page under the non-delta ordering. Never a 500, never a 400, never a forced-empty list. An offset-less but valid ISO8601 instant is accepted as UTC. The delta boundary is also widened backwards by the bounded commit-lag epsilon (5s), so the effective filter is > since - 5s.
acceptance_criteria_amendments.rationale: DELIBERATE AS-BUILT DECISION, not an unfixed finding — the spec is what was wrong. (#428's proposal, quoted for the record: a malformed since should 'return an empty result or 400, never a 500'.) #428's HARD requirement (never a 500) HOLDS; its 'empty result or 400' wording does not, and the shipped behavior is kept on purpose. since is a delta-read OPTIMIZATION on a FAIL-OPEN SessionStart path: returning the newest page on a bad since is strictly safer for that consumer than a 400, which would blank the TEAM CHANNEL block entirely and give a session less context than it had before. A forced-empty result would be equally wrong — it would look like 'nothing happened on this repo'. normalize_since/1 (lib/loopctl/coordination.ex:2207-2221) resolves once, so the filter (apply_since/2, :2223-2232) and the ordering (order_recent/2, :2286-2295) can never disagree about the delta mode. The one case NOT degraded is an offset-less-but-valid instant: parse_since/1 (:2297+) accepts it as UTC because DateTime.from_iso8601/1 rejects it, and silently dropping the filter there would return the whole channel and defeat 'read only what's new'. Also restated for precision: a RESOLVED since is not applied verbatim — the caller widens it by commit_lag_since/1 (coordination.ex:1813, helper :2239-2242, @commit_lag_epsilon_seconds = 5 at :142), so the effective boundary is > since - 5s (at-least-once overlap for commit lag, AC-40.C2.2); a test derived from the literal '> since' would wrongly assert that a row touched at since-3s is excluded.

test_cases.name: returns own project's live posts newest-first
since returns only the delta
preconditions: posts at t1 and t3; since=t2

test_cases.name: cross-tenant AND nonexistent project both 200 empty (no oracle)
steps: GET with a random nonexistent UUID
expected_results: both 200 with empty data, identical responses

test_cases.name: delta ordering by GREATEST keeps a re-touched slot inside the LIMIT window (#428 regression guard)
preconditions: a keyed slot whose inserted_at PREDATES since but whose updated_at is the most recent touch
two ordinary posts inserted AFTER since but BEFORE the slot's touch
read with since set and limit 2
expected_results: the re-touched slot is returned FIRST (not truncated out by its stale inserted_at)
result is [slot, p2] — the delta branch of order_recent/2, per AC-39.3.1
test_cases.note: Shipped guard: test/loopctl/coordination_test.exs:399 'delta ORDER BY GREATEST keeps a re-touched slot from being truncated by limit' (and :607 for recent_page/3).

test_cases.name: a malformed since is a NO-OP filter, never an error (AC-39.3.3)
preconditions: one old post and one new post on the channel
expected_results: both return the FULL newest-first page (old and new) — the filter degrades to a no-op
no raise, no 500, no 400, no forced-empty list
test_cases.note: Shipped guard: test/loopctl/coordination_test.exs:356 'a malformed since string is a no-op filter (not an error)'; the offset-less-but-valid instant case is the sibling test at :350.

technical_notes: Context: Loopctl.Coordination.recent(tenant_id, project_id, opts) — AdminRepo query filtering tenant_id + project_id + expires_at > now(), limit clamped to 100 (@default_recent_limit 25 / @max_recent_limit 100, coordination.ex:60-61).

Ordering is CONDITIONAL (order_recent/2, coordination.ex:2286-2295): non-delta (no since, or a cursor present) => inserted_at DESC, seq DESC; delta (since present AND no cursor) => GREATEST(inserted_at, updated_at) DESC, seq DESC, matching the apply_since/2 filter (:2223-2232) so a re-upserted keyed slot is not truncated out of the LIMIT window by its stale inserted_at. seq is the tie-breaker: a DB-side bigserial mapped as field :seq, :integer, read_after_writes: true (channel_post.ex:198-201). Epic 40's cursor NULLs since when present (recent_page/3, coordination.ex:1806), so cursor+since is a history read. Do NOT unify the branches — same split Epic 40 documents at us_40.c2.json AC-40.C2.4.

Malformed/absent/date-only since => nil => no-op filter => newest page under the non-delta ordering (normalize_since/1, coordination.ex:2207-2221). Never a 400 or 500: since is a delta optimization on a fail-open SessionStart path. An offset-less but valid ISO8601 instant is parsed as UTC (parse_since/1, :2297+).
Oracle-safety: return {:ok, []} for a project the tenant doesn't own — do NOT branch to :not_found. This keeps cross-tenant existence unobservable and simplifies the consumer.
Do NOT self-dedup server-side — that is the consumer's job (US-39.6).
This GET is NOT covered by require_human_anchor_default_deny_test (it only walks POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) — no allowlist entry needed (correcting the earlier note).
Emit a security-event log on any internal error but never leak cross-tenant existence.
